// why: The register of the mutation run (req-quality-unit). It holds what cannot be read out of Stryker's report: WHICH files are to be measured, WHAT score is the floor and WHICH narrowings of the denominator are deliberate. The gate `tools/check-mutation.mjs` compares this file against the report, that is against what the run REALLY did — not against the configuration that declares it.
// patterns: A copy of `mutate` from `stryker.config.json`, written out here so that changing it is a comparison rather than an act of trust. Narrowing the pattern is the cheapest way of raising the score: a file struck from the measurement takes its surviving mutants with it and the percentage rises although no test was added. The same defect as `coverageInclude` in `lesson-45`, one floor up. The list names what is NOT measured rather than what is: as an allow-list every new file landed outside the measurement by default and silently, which is the state `unmeasured` and the gate's `source-unaccounted` were written against.
// files: The inventory outright: what is to be measured. The patterns above watch that nobody narrowed the measurement; this list watches that a file covered by a pattern really entered the report. Neither is enough alone — a pattern can stay untouched while a file disappears (a rename, a move), and the score rises by itself again.
// noMutants: A file inside the measurement out of which Stryker can make not one mutant does NOT appear in the report. Without this list it would be indistinguishable from a file that dropped out of the measurement — and those are two different things, only one of them in order. An entry requires a reason and stops being true on the day the file gets its first mutant: the gate fires then.

noMutants.reason: An empty class under a decorator: `PctContainer {}` is a selector, a template of one slot and a host class, all of it metadata Stryker leaves alone. The component's whole behaviour is `container.scss` reading its tokens, and behaviour written in CSS is measured by the e2e ruler (`layout.spec.ts` reads the column's width at three viewports), not by mutants. Zero is the correct result of the measurement, and the day the class grows a first member this entry stops being true and the gate fires.

One exported union of four string literals and nothing else: `PctTone` is a TYPE, and a type is gone at compilation. There is no condition here, no runtime literal, no call with an argument — the four names live on in the components that take the input, and that is where their mutants are thrown. Zero is the correct result of the measurement, not its absence.

The file carries the type `PctCompareWith` and one assignment, `export const pctSameValue = Object.is`. The type vanishes at compilation, and assigning a reference to a built-in function has nothing to mutate: there is no condition here, no literal, no call with an argument. Zero mutants is the correct result of the measurement here, not the absence of one.

Two directives with an EMPTY body: `PctLabelAux` and `PctMessageAux` are a selector and a `data-pct-part` each, and both of those live in the decorator, which Stryker leaves alone. There is no condition here, no call and no literal outside the metadata, so zero mutants is the correct result of the measurement rather than the absence of one — what the two really promise is a slot in `field.html`, and that is `check-parts`.

The same shape as the container for the same reason: `PctGrid {}` is decorator metadata around an empty body, and the one declaration that IS the component — the auto-fit `grid-template-columns` — lives in `grid.scss`, where the e2e ruler counts real columns at three widths. There is nothing here for Stryker to hold, and this entry expires with the first member the class grows.

One directive whose entire runtime is the decorator's host binding spelling `pctTheme()` onto `data-theme` (0059: the mechanism stays the cascade), plus a type and `readonly pctTheme = input.required<PctThemeName | null>()` — a call with no argument to mutate, assigned to a field with no condition around it. What the directive promises is measured where it acts: three unit cases on the rendered attribute and the sandbox e2e reading `--pct-surface` through both writers. Zero mutants is the measurement's correct answer, not a gap in it.

// unmeasured: The register of what is deliberately NOT measured, and why. `patterns` and `files` watch that nothing DROPS OUT of the measurement; neither of them can say anything about a file that was never in — and that was the default state of every new file, because a pattern names what is measured. The gate reads the library's sources off the git index and requires each of them to stand either in `files` or here. An entry here does not say "this file scores poorly", it says "this file cannot be measured" — and the reason has to say what stops it, because that sentence is the whole of the entry.

unmeasured.reason: Instrumented, the file brings the INITIAL TEST RUN down, and with it the whole run rather than its own score. Measured: with `affix.ts` in `mutate`, `field.spec.ts` reads `data-pct-fit="inset"` where the fixture writes `pctPrefix="fill"`. Stryker instruments the `input()` configuration object BEFORE the `angular` ignorer strikes its mutants out of the score, so the alias stops being a literal the compiler can read, and a static attribute carrying a value stops being an input binding — it stays an attribute and the input keeps its default. The library's other aliased inputs (`icon`, `popover`, `tooltip`, `overlay`) are measured because no spec of theirs sets one as a plain attribute with a value. This is not a file with a low score; it is a file the measurement cannot hold, and 14 mutants is what it costs.

// coversNothing: The register of specs that RUN in the mutation run and cover no mutant. Stryker's per-test report lists only the tests that cover one, so a spec whose whole subject stands outside `patterns` is absent from it — and point 3 cannot tell that apart from a spec the run never saw. An entry here does not say "this spec matters less"; it says "this spec can kill nothing, and here is what it holds instead". The register exists because the cheap way to keep point 3 green would be to widen the measurement until the spec covers something, which is the move this whole file refuses.
// equivalent: The fourth register, and the only one about a MUTANT rather than a file: a survivor the suite cannot tell from the original. It is keyed on the operator, the span and the replacement, so an entry dies with the line it excuses rather than drifting onto the next mutant to take that place. Nothing here excuses a score: a registered mutant is still counted as surviving, because it is. What the entry buys is that the next reader does not re-derive the argument — and proving one by hand has two traps, both met in this repository (`lesson-199`): the edit must be one the compiler accepts, and a kill by hand can still be reported as a survivor. An entry is red the day the run kills the mutant, the day the line moves, and the day it carries no sentence.

equivalent.reason: `if (key === null || event.key !== key) return` with the LEFT operand forced false. The right one answers for both: `key` is `string | null` and `event.key` is a `DOMString`, so whenever `key` is null, `event.key !== key` is true and the guard returns by the other road. Equivalent RELATIVE TO THE PLATFORM's type — a case could forge `key: null` onto the event and tell them apart, and it would be asserting on a state a `KeyboardEvent` cannot reach. The entry expires the day `PctRegionsApi.key` can hold something a `DOMString` can equal.

The `?.` on a receiver that is provably not null here. `regions` is `private readonly regions = inject(PCT_REGIONS)`, set once and never reassigned, and the guard two lines up returns when it is null — so on every path reaching this line the optional chain has nothing to guard. The strongest of the four: no test distinguishes them because the mutated expression is never evaluated with a null receiver. Note the neighbour: the same `?.` removed one line earlier IS reachable, and the run reports it as an errored mutant rather than a survivor.

`if (holding === this.holding) return` never returning, so `sync()` tells the service on every pointer and focus event instead of on a change. Nothing downstream moves: `hold()` opens with `if (this.held) return` and `release()` with `if (!this.held) return`, so a repeat is a no-op in both directions and no clock is re-armed. A spy counting calls would see the difference, which is a count rather than a behaviour. The entry expires the day either method stops being idempotent — and the guard stays, because it is what makes the counting independent of that.

The `'host'` default of `listenOn`, replaced by the empty string. It has exactly one reader in the whole library — `if (this.listenOn() !== 'document') return` — so every string but that one takes the same branch, installs no listener and leaves no trace on the element. The only case that could separate them reads the signal's own value, which asserts on a constant rather than on what the directive does. The entry expires the moment a second reader appears, or the moment the predicate is written the other way round.

// threshold: The hard floor of the score for the whole, in percent. The same number stands in `thresholds.break` in `stryker.config.json` and the gate watches that the two agree — because that one fails the run and this one is its only justification. `break` is `null` by Stryker's own default, so BY DEFAULT the mutation run exits zero whatever the score and is a report to look at.
// tolerance: By how many percentage points a file's score may drift from the snapshot before it is a change requiring a decision. Checked BOTH WAYS: downwards, because that is what a removed assertion looks like; upwards, because a floor standing ten points below the measurement stops measuring anything — one could then delete every fifth assertion and stay green. The price is written down outright: improving the tests requires rewriting the snapshot (`--write`), that is a line in the diff visible in review.
// ignorers: Stryker plugins that STRIKE mutants out of the denominator (status `Ignored`). Each has to stand here together with a reason, because each raises the score without adding a single test. The gate compares this list against what the report declares as used, and checks separately that NO ignored mutant carries a reason from outside this list — that is how `// Stryker disable` comments, invisible in the configuration, enter the repository.

mutantReasons: Angular signal based input, model and output functions configuration object cannot be mutated as that causes issues with the Angular compiler.
Angular signal query options object cannot be mutated as that causes issues with the Angular compiler.
angular.reason: The configuration object of `input()`, `model()`, `output()` and of the view queries is read STATICALLY by the Angular compiler. Mutated, it stops being a literal, so ngtsc does not compile the component at all — the whole file falls back to JIT and brings the dry run down with `Component 'PctSelect' is not resolved`. This is not a mutant the tests failed to kill, it is a mutant that cannot be run. TWO texts and not one: the plugin words the QUERY case differently, and the second sentence arrived with the first `contentChildren()` in a measured file — until then the register looked complete, and the new wording read exactly like a `// Stryker disable` comment somebody had smuggled in.

// clock: A mutant killed by the CLOCK counts towards the score exactly like one killed by an assertion. Shortening the limits is therefore a way of raising the percentage without writing tests, and a long tail of timeouts means the score is being bought with the clock. `minimumMS` and `minimumFactor` are lower bounds on Stryker's settings, `clockShare` — the upper bound on the share of timeouts among the killed, in percent.
